name: Marpac Medical
about:
Marpac Medical operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it has produced medical devices since its spin-off from Rotec in 1992. Rotec began in the 1980s manufacturing tracheostomy tube holders and orthopedic products for DePuy; when DePuy acquired the orthopedic division, the tracheostomy holder business became the privately held Marpac.

The company manufactures FDA Class 1 medical devices, specifically endotracheal (ET) tube holders and tracheostomy tube holders. All products are designed and produced at its Albuquerque facility without outsourcing, a structure the company says allows strict quality control and rapid response to customer needs. Marpac aims to keep all items in stock and typically ships orders within one to two days.

Marpac serves the medical community, including hospitals, clinicians, and home-care patients. Its distributor network includes New Start Home Medical Equipment, Timberlake Medical, Affordable Medical Supply, and Medical Specialties Distributors.

Founded on principles of quality, affordability, innovation, and customer service, Marpac was created to develop products that improve patient care while remaining easy for medical staff and families to use.

name: Mars Plastics
old_description: Impeccable Customer Service with each customer assigned their own inside representative
about:
Mars Plastics operates from Providence, Rhode Island, with a second facility in nearby Cranston. The company has over 50 years of injection molding experience and remains a family-owned business passed through generations. Founded as a molding operation, it has grown into one of the largest injection molders on the East Coast, serving customers ranging from individual inventors to major retailers.

The company runs a 100,000-square-foot facility operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its equipment lineup includes 40 injection molding machines — 36 in Providence and four in Cranston — ranging from 12 to 1,400 tons of clamping force with shot capacities up to 160 ounces. Core processes cover conventional injection molding, gas-assist molding, over-molding, insert molding, and two-color molding. In-house capabilities extend to tool design and machining, design engineering with CAD and simulation, finishing (trimming, painting, printing, plating), assembly, and work-cell manufacturing that integrates decorating and packaging. A recent addition is 3D printing for rapid prototyping and low-volume production.

Mars Plastics serves retail giants such as Target and Walmart as an authorized manufacturer, along with a broad base of corporate clients and startup inventors. The company has helped numerous small concepts scale into industry leaders and has guided established corporations in reshoring production from overseas to its Rhode Island plants. Its contract manufacturing services support third-party brands across consumer goods and other sectors.

The company emphasizes a dedicated inside representative for every customer, continuous reinvestment in new molding machines and robotic automation, and a quality system that retains first and last shots from each run alongside statistical process control. Work-cell manufacturing is cited as a key differentiator that allows Mars to compete with overseas facilities on cost and lead time.

name: Martel Inc
old_description: Excellent service over the last 15 years. When we have an issue with our phones / cables / video equipment they are very timely and friendly in their service.
about:
Martel Inc was founded on July 2, 1984, in Dover, Delaware, by Mark B. Carlson. The family-owned company began as a one-man operation out of a garage, aiming to provide reliable telecommunications solutions for businesses on the Delmarva Peninsula.

Today, Martel operates from a commercial facility in Dover with a fully stocked parts warehouse and offers 24/7 service. The company provides cloud-based VOIP, legacy telecommunications, video surveillance systems, access control, and structured cabling for computer and telephone networks. A full staff of technicians and sales personnel handles installation, maintenance, and support.

Martel serves businesses across Delmarva and southeastern Pennsylvania, including clients such as Delaware Grange Mutual Insurance Company, Parsell Funeral Homes & Crematorium, Surgical Associates, and the Delaware Surgery Center. Its customer base spans industries needing commercial phone systems, security cameras, legacy telecom, and network cabling.

The founder started the business to fill a gap for reputable, responsive telecom service. The company emphasizes an old-fashioned, live customer-service approach—personalized, prompt, and focused on solving problems—as its primary differentiator against larger national competitors.

name: Martin's Furniture
old_description: Check out these products from our most popular categories of furniture.
about:
Martin's Furniture is a family-owned business based in Ephrata, Pennsylvania, operated by Marlin and his family. The company runs a retail showroom and a workshop where it produces custom furniture, upholstery, and finishing work alongside a curated selection of branded lines.

The store carries collections from makers such as Zimmerman Chair, Lancaster Legacy, Barkman Furniture, Buckeye Seating, and Grand Slabs, offering dining tables, counter chairs, porch furniture, and live-edge slabs paired with steel bases. In-house capabilities include custom furniture design, custom upholstery, custom finishing, and the fabrication of live-edge tables and replacement parts. A white-glove delivery service handles professional handling, room-of-choice placement, assembly, setup, and packaging removal.

Customers range from homeowners furnishing primary residences to buyers seeking heirloom-quality pieces; testimonials cite a 2.5-hour drive from New Jersey for dining sets, same-day replacement parts for a 20-year-old glider, and custom butcher-block countertops in multiple hardwoods. The shop serves both retail walk-ins and custom-order clients.

The company emphasizes handcrafted construction using sustainably sourced hardwoods and Amish-built pieces, positioning its white-glove service and in-house customization as key differentiators for buyers who want tailored, durable furniture without managing multiple vendors.

name: Maryland Community Solar
old_description: Join Maryland Community Solar and save 5% to 25% on your electric bill.
about:
Maryland Community Solar operates from Columbia, Maryland, as a locally owned, family-run enterprise led by CEO Tony Napolitano. The company was established to educate Maryland residents and businesses about community solar programs and to simplify enrollment in those programs.

The firm provides consumer education on the benefits of community solar, assesses eligibility, and guides customers through the enrollment process. A customer relations team works directly with homeowners, renters, and businesses, including those served by third-party energy suppliers, to explain how subscription to a local solar farm can reduce electric bills by 5% to 25%. The company reports assisting hundreds of customers across the state.

Services are directed at Maryland residential and commercial utility customers who cannot install rooftop panels, such as condominium dwellers, as well as businesses seeking renewable energy credits. The company coordinates with solar developers and utility providers to facilitate the subscription and billing process.

The organization states its mission is to make Maryland a leader in sustainability and renewable energy through honest communication, by example, and caring for customers and communities.

name: Maryland Food Center Authority
old_description: This merchant provides a variety of produce. Please contact them directly for current offerings.
about:
The Maryland Food Center Authority (MFCA) operates from Jessup, Maryland, where it oversees the Maryland Food Center, a centralized hub for wholesale food distribution. Established as a state authority, the MFCA is tasked with developing, owning, and maintaining real estate projects that support the region’s food supply chain.

The authority manages two primary facilities—the Maryland Wholesale Produce Market and the Maryland Market Center—leasing space to a roster of wholesale merchants selling fruits, vegetables, and seafood. Its role is facility development and property management rather than food production; it provides sanitary, modern infrastructure and services such as stormwater management and a truck wash for tenants.

The center serves the broader food industry, including wholesale produce distributors, seafood suppliers, and a single retail seafood vendor open to the public. Tenants such as Pro Produce, C&D Produce, Sweet Seasons Maryland, War Shore Trading Company, Wild Seafood, and Viva Food operate within the leased units, distributing products regionally.

The MFCA’s mission is to maximize the efficiency of Maryland’s food distribution network and ensure the state’s future food supply through coordinated public-private development. Its vision aims for the most modern, safe, and efficient food distribution network in the world.

name: Maryland Medical Devices
old_description: *Maryland Medical Devices* is dedicated to the distribution of high quality  medical devices developed specifically for the orthopedic segment of healthcare.
about:
Maryland Medical Devices, based in Crofton, Maryland, was founded in 2010 as a privately held company. The firm operates from a suite on Espey Court and focuses exclusively on the orthopedic implant market.

The company distributes and markets orthopedic products, specializing in total joint arthroplasty, sports medicine, and intramedullary fixation devices for minimally invasive surgical procedures. It does not manufacture its own devices; instead, it relies on manufacturing partners to develop solutions that are less invasive, more cost effective, and reduce operating-room time. Product lines referenced include the Apex Knee, Trauma, and Gallileo systems.

Maryland Medical Devices serves the orthopedic segment of healthcare, selling to surgeons, hospitals, and sales agents within the orthopedic community. Its management team brings combined experience across all aspects of the orthopedic market, and the company emphasizes education for both its sales agents and clinical customers.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a commitment to excellence, high-quality products and service, and a leadership role in education. It builds on strong customer relationships and manufacturer expertise to improve every aspect of its business, aiming to deliver precise, reproducible surgical solutions without compromise to the patient.

about:
Maryland Parts operates from Beltsville, Maryland, as an auto parts dealer serving customers through its e-commerce website. The company does not disclose a founding year, ownership structure, or founder names in its public materials.

The business stocks and sells replacement body components for a broad range of vehicle makes and models, including Ford, Nissan, Toyota, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Chevrolet, and others. Its catalog covers bumpers, fenders, doors, hoods, grilles, headlights, tail lights, fog lights, radiators, radiator supports, mirrors, and related trim pieces. Orders are fulfilled via online checkout with major credit cards accepted, and the company notes that shipping is available island-wide, though service is excluded for New York Boroughs and certain other cities.

Maryland Parts serves the automotive aftermarket, supplying parts to both professional repair shops and individual vehicle owners. The product listings reference specific model years for popular platforms such as the Ford Transit, Nissan Sentra, Toyota Camry, Honda Accord, and Honda CR-V, indicating a focus on late-model collision and maintenance needs.

The company highlights its customer service, a 30-day free return policy, a rewards program, and secured payment processing as key differentiators. These policies are presented as the primary reasons customers choose the retailer over alternatives.

about:
Mastro Electric Supply Co. Inc. was founded in 1946 in Providence, Rhode Island. The company operates as an independent electrical supply and lighting retailer with its main showroom on Elmwood Avenue. No founder names or ownership details are disclosed in public sources.

The business stocks and sells lighting fixtures, systems, and electrical components for residential and commercial projects. It also provides lighting design services and product consulting through its showrooms. The company maintains four locations: a flagship in Providence, a branch in Pawcatuck, Connecticut, and two additional showrooms in Middletown and Wakefield, Rhode Island. It describes itself as the largest independent lighting retailer in the state.

Customers include homeowners, electrical contractors, and commercial builders seeking lighting and electrical supplies. The retailer serves both walk-in retail traffic and trade accounts, offering design assistance and help locating hard-to-find items.

Mastro Electric emphasizes a satisfaction guarantee, knowledgeable staff, and competitive pricing as its distinguishing factors. The company states it will go out of its way to source products not in stock, positioning itself as a full-service lighting resource rather than a simple distributor.
